assets.video.bitrate.mode.matched: 720p50, preferably as (Avid) DNxHD 175x (a.k.a. 185x), optionally as (Panasonic) AVC-Intra 100, optionally as (Apple) ProRes 422 (HQ), all 10-bit video codecs, and optionally as (Sony) XDCAM MPEG HD422, 8-bit (§5.2.1)
assets.video.bitrate.mode.note: the document names four alternative HD delivery codecs per frame-rate/resolution combination (DNxHD, AVC-Intra 100, ProRes 422 HQ, XDCAM MPEG HD422) without stating one shared delivery bitrate; §1.6.1 gives only a 160 Mb/s floor for intra-frame post-production codecs generally, not a fixed or capped delivery rate. Derived: bitrate.mode=unconstrained because no single number applies across the allowed codec set.

assets.video.frame_rate.mode.matched: 50 frames per second, progressive scan – known as 720p/50 ... 25 frames per second (50 fields) interlaced – known as 1080i/25 ... 25 frames per second, progressive scan ... known as 1080p/25 (§1.1.2)
assets.video.frame_rate.mode.note: the document names exactly two discrete frame rates (25 and 50 fps) rather than a continuous range, so the schema's frame_rate.mode is derived as 'allowed_list' rather than 'range' — same pattern as clearcast_commercials' frame_rate.mode record.

assets.video.gop.max_length.matched: 720p50, preferably as (Avid) DNxHD 175x ... optionally as (Panasonic) AVC-Intra 100, optionally as (Apple) ProRes 422 (HQ) ... optionally as (Sony) XDCAM MPEG HD422 (§5.2.1); 'Intra-frame based post-production codecs used to edit HD programmes should be at least 160 Mb/s' (§1.6.1)
assets.video.gop.max_length.note: the document never uses the word GOP. All the HD delivery codecs it names (DNxHD, AVC-Intra 100, ProRes 422 HQ, XDCAM MPEG HD422) are intra-frame-only professional formats, and §1.6.1 independently frames 'intra-frame based' codecs as the expected class for HD post-production. Derived: an all-intra codec set implies GOP max_length=1 (every frame independently coded). Flag for human review — inferred from the codec list, not a stated GOP value.

assets.audio.codec.disallowed[1].matched: Audio that has previously been lossy bit reduced must not be used, due to causing cascade coding artefacts. (§2.x, before 2.8 Sound to Vision Synchronisation)
assets.audio.codec.disallowed[1].note: mp3 is not literally named; it is a lossy audio codec and therefore falls under this general prohibition on previously lossy-bit-reduced audio — the same source sentence already recorded (via method=literal) for disallowed[0]/[2] (aac/ac3).

constraints.timing.duration.tolerance_ms.matched: a 25-counting timecode (25 T/C) must be used (§5.4); 'File duration and timecode must exactly match the principal video file' (§4.8)
constraints.timing.duration.tolerance_ms.note: 40ms = one video frame at the document's own 25fps timecode counting rate. Not a number the document states directly — derived from how strictly it treats exact duration/timecode matching (audio-only files must exactly match the principal video file; hard-parted programme metadata requires exact part durations). Flag for human review before trusting as a hard tolerance — same derivation pattern as clearcast_commercials' duration.tolerance_ms.
